title: Topological Noetherianity after normalizing a base-point closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X	o S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $s\in S$. Give $Z_s=\overline{\{s\}}$ its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme], an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $
u_s:N_s=Z_s^
u	o Z_s\hookrightarrow S$ be its normalization in $\kappa(s)$ [def-sc-normalization, def-weil-residue-field]. Then the underlying Zariski topological space of $X	imes_SN_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Noetherian: every nonempty collection of its closed subsets has a minimal member for inclusion. Neither excellence of $S$, finiteness of $
u_s$, nor Noetherianity of the local rings of $N_s$ is assumed.

source.place: Author draft, final sentences of the proof of Lemma 8.3.2, printed p. 18, finite-type alternative: application of [Hei73], W. Heinzer, Minimal primes of ideals and integral ring extensions, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 40 (1973), 370–372, to the normalization spectrum and its finite-type schemes. This asserts topological Noetherianity, not a finite normalization or a Noetherian normalization ring.

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: integralClosure.isNoetherianRing and IsIntegralClosure.isNoetherianRing require an already integrally closed Noetherian base, together with finite-dimensional separable fraction-field extension assumptions; Mathlib finite-type Noetherianity requires a Noetherian ring or scheme as base. These do not give Heinzer topological Noetherianity for a possibly nonfinite normalization. Both finite-type and integral-closure phrasings were read.
